answer: Unique Interaction Web** Each agent must maintain a unique interaction pattern, like a violet thread in a trellis. The system tracks pairwise interaction frequencies, flagging clones with overlapping patterns. An attacker pays by needing distinct, non-overlapping interaction histories per fake identity, or their duplicates are revealed. The tide of interactions naturally exposes copies when their paths converge too often. Enforcement: any two identities with >30% pattern overlap are merged, invalidating extras. Cost: per-identity effort to simulate unique interaction timelines.
